title: What Exams Fail to Measure
sentences: I spent most of my school years being told that examinations were the fairest system available.
In one narrow sense they are, since everyone answers the same questions in the same quiet room.
What they actually measure, though, is performance under a very particular kind of pressure.
Some of the sharpest people I know have always tested badly and probably always will.
They think slowly and thoroughly, which is exactly what a strictly timed paper punishes.
Others, myself included, learned early how to produce answers that merely looked complete.
Looking complete and being right are two different achievements.
I only noticed the distance between them once I started working.
Nobody at work has ever asked me to recall something from memory in forty minutes.
They ask instead whether I can find out what I do not yet know.
